plain_english: Then the existence of the circle is briefly described: having established the eastern direction, one stretches the thread uniformly.
sanskrit_cite: atha maṇḍalasadbhāvaḥ saṃkṣepeṇābhidhīyate sādhayitvā diśaṃ pūrvāṃ sūtramāsphālayetsamam

plain_english: Having halved that, one marks again in middle, east, and west; then by half-of-half measure, east and west.
sanskrit_cite: tadardhayitvā madhyaprākpratīcīṣvaṅkayetpunaḥ tato@pyardhatadardhārdhamānataḥ pūrvapaścimau

plain_english: By that much one marks; with thread one gives the twin compass; the fish-joint pair thus becomes in south and north.
sanskrit_cite: aṅkayettāvatā dadyāt sūtreṇa bhramayugmakam matsyasandhidvayaṃ tvevaṃ dakṣiṇottarayorbhavet

plain_english: In its middle one drops the thread for south-north success; or, with an east-west equal thread, north-south.
sanskrit_cite: tanmadhye pātayetsūtraṃ dakṣiṇottarasiddhaye yadi vā prākparāktulyasūtreṇottaradakṣiṇe

plain_english: One marks from the other mark and from the east too; likewise those are placed in the fish middle, throwing a long thread south-north.
sanskrit_cite: aṅkayedaparādaṅkāt pūrvādapi tathaiva te matsyamadhye kṣipetsūtramāyataṃ dakṣiṇottare

plain_english: By the measured field's half measure, from the middle one marks toward directions; with two threads arising from two directions, the fish becomes corner-placed.
sanskrit_cite: matakṣetrārdhamānena madhyāddikṣvaṅkayettataḥ sūtrābhyāṃ digdvayotthābhyāṃ matsyaḥ syātpratikoṇagaḥ

plain_english: In the fishes, the Vedas are threads; thus a square is proclaimed, from one onward, as a hundred-ending mandala.
sanskrit_cite: matsyeṣu vedāḥ sūtrāṇītyevaṃ syāccaturasrakam ekasmātprabhṛti proktaṃ śatāntaṃ maṇḍalaṃ yataḥ

plain_english: In the Siddhanta tantra, a hundred mandalas are called that seat; what goes in its middle, the chief three mandalas, is remembered.
sanskrit_cite: siddhātantre maṇḍalānāṃ śataṃ tatpīṭha ucyate yattanmadhyagataṃ mukhyaṃ maṇḍalānāṃ trayaṃ smṛtam

plain_english: Middle trident, triple trident, and nine trident are clear; there the trident arrangement is said with infinite divisions.
sanskrit_cite: madhyaśūlaṃ tritriśūlaṃ navaśūlamiti sphuṭam tatra śūlavidhānaṃ yaduktaṃ bhedairanantakaiḥ

plain_english: We say that yoni mandala, shown by the order of true being; in the four-handed Veda-supported form, abandon three parts all around.
sanskrit_cite: tadyoni maṇḍalaṃ brūmaḥ sadbhāvakramadarśitam vedāśrite caturhaste tribhāgaṃ sarvatastyajet

plain_english: Divide all each field by sixteen parts; then the middle of two brahma threads is clearly the brahma place.
sanskrit_cite: bhāgaiḥ ṣoḍaśabhiḥ sarvaṃ tattatkṣetraṃ vibhājayet brahmasūtradvayasyātha madhyaṃ brahmapadaṃ sphuṭam

plain_english: Having made a boundary, then the target is the fourth thread from the beginning; then go transversely to the fourth thread thereafter.
sanskrit_cite: kṛtvāvadhiṃ tato lakṣyaṃ caturthaṃ sūtramāditaḥ tatastiryagvrajet sūtraṃ caturthaṃ tadanantare

plain_english: In the square, if there are two moons, make the outer half-part; their attached brahma-sutra is situated at the third marman.
sanskrit_cite: koṣṭhe cendudvayaṃ kuryādbahirbhāgārdhabhāgataḥ tayorlagnaṃ brahmasūtrāttṛtīye marmaṇi sthitam

plain_english: If so, in the half of the square, the inward-facing pair would be at the second marman of the hand, immovable.
sanskrit_cite: koṣṭhakārdhe@paraṃ ceti yugmamantarmukhaṃ bhavet brahmasūtrāddvitīyasmin haste marmaṇi niścalam

plain_english: Having made a pair of full moons, the wise one should turn them from the sixth brahma-sutra point to the third cross part.
sanskrit_cite: kṛtvā pūrṇenduyugalaṃ vartayeta vicakṣaṇaḥ brahmasūtragatāt ṣaṣṭhāt tiryagbhāgāttṛtīyake

plain_english: Having made a half-square, rotate the thread hanging from the full moon tip, upward-facing, toward the broken-moon pair fire part.
sanskrit_cite: kṛtvārdhakoṣṭhake sūtraṃ pūrṇacandrāgralambitam bhramayedunmukhaṃ khaṇḍacandrayugvahnibhāgagam

plain_english: Having abandoned the cross-part pair, from the western broken moon then to the corner, so it would be; make a broken piece with two rotations.
sanskrit_cite: tiryagbhāgadvayaṃ tyaktvā khaṇḍendoḥ paścimāttataḥ koṇaṃ yāvattathā syācca kuryāt khaṇḍaṃ bhramadvayam

plain_english: From that one very sharp curved tip a horn is born; the same rule is declared for the second; this rule is clear.
sanskrit_cite: sutīkṣṇakuṭilāgraṃ tadekaṃ śṛṅgaṃ prajāyate dvitīyasminnapi proktaḥ śṛṅga eṣa vidhiḥ sphuṭaḥ

plain_english: When the middle horn is to be made, in the third upper square and fourth half, an inward-facing pair of moon-halves would be.
sanskrit_cite: madhyaśṛṅge@tha kartavye tṛtīye ūrdhvakoṣṭhake caturthārdhe ca candrārdhadvayamantarmukhaṃ bhavet

plain_english: And that one full moon, previously turned, should reach as needed; by mutual knot union a bound state arises.
sanskrit_cite: tacca pūrṇendumekaṃ prāgvartitaṃ prāpnuyādyathā anyonyagranthiyogena baddhāratvaṃ prajāyate

plain_english: Thus on the second side, from turning the broken-moon pair, the joined cheek-knot should be led forward by the other two middles.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ dvitīyapārśve@sya khaṇḍendudvayavartanāt madhyābhyāṃ gaṇḍikā śliṣṭā parābhyāmagrato nayet

plain_english: The thread in both sides, by which it becomes sharp and goes to the middle horn, has the second brahma-sutra behind at the bottom of both sides.
sanskrit_cite: sūtraṃ pārśvadvaye yena tīkṣṇaṃ syānmadhyaśṛṅgagam pārśvadvayādhare paścādbrahmasūtraṃ dvitīyakam

plain_english: With attention it should be grasped by the teacher who knows the ritual; the mantra-knower would be rear-facing in that brahma-sutra.
sanskrit_cite: avadhānena saṃgrāhyamācāryeṇohavedinā bhavetpaścānmukho mantrī tasmiṃśca brahmasūtrake

plain_english: Having excluded the middle horn, all the previously stated rule then applies to the upward-facing broken-moon pair previously declared.
sanskrit_cite: madhyaśṛṅgaṃ varjayitvā sarvaḥ pūrvodito vidhiḥ tato yadunmukhaṃ khaṇḍacandrayugmaṃ puroditam

plain_english: Then, by two, the gandika well fitted inside, by two front threads, the middle horn pair becomes.
sanskrit_cite: tato dvayena kartavyā gaṇḍikāntaḥsusaṃgatā dvayenāgragasūtrābhyāṃ madhyaśṛṅgadvayaṃ bhavet

plain_english: Below, by increase of its part, the lotus has four circles; then the wheel is sixteen-spoked or twelve-spoked, in two ways.
sanskrit_cite: adho bhāgavivṛddhyāsya padmaṃ vṛttacatuṣṭayam tataścakraṃ ṣoḍaśāraṃ dvādaśāraṃ dvidhātha tat

plain_english: In the middle, the place of Kuleshvari may be space, or tilaka, or lotus, or a six-spoked wheel, or a twelvefold space.
sanskrit_cite: madhye kuleśvarīsthānaṃ vyoma vā tilakaṃ ca vā padmaṃ vātha ṣaḍaraṃ vā viyaddvādaśakaṃ ca vā

plain_english: At the trident, seven-spoked, by mere joining from the middle, of lotuses then wheels or spaces, seven becomes.
sanskrit_cite: tritriśūle@tra saptāre śliṣṭamātreṇa madhyataḥ padmānāmatha cakrāṇāṃ vyomnāṃ vā saptakaṃ bhavet

plain_english: Mixed or confused by difference of contraction and expansion; then by half-measure of field, one should throw the field there with extra measure.
sanskrit_cite: miśritaṃ vātha saṃkīrṇaṃ samāsavyāsabhedataḥ tataḥ kṣetrārdhamānena kṣetraṃ tatrādhikaṃ kṣipet

plain_english: There the staff is remembered: a part of six-spoked pure essence, very sharp-tipped, red-glowing, causing instant possession.
sanskrit_cite: tatra daṇḍaḥ smṛto bhāgaḥ ṣaḍarāmalasārakaḥ sutīkṣṇāgraḥ suraktābhaḥ kṣaṇādāveśakārakaḥ

plain_english: That goddess Kundalini, called wave and great-wave-possessing, is situated in the kanda called six-cornered and is six-deity-natured.
sanskrit_cite: yā sā kuṇḍalinī devī taraṅgākhyā mahormiṇī sā ṣaḍaśreṇa kandākhye sthitā ṣaḍdevatātmikā

plain_english: Spread out and long by eight parts, from half of that; then doors should be made in order by variegated turning.
sanskrit_cite: aṣṭabhāgaiśca vistīrṇo dīrghaścāpi tadardhataḥ tato dvārāṇi kāryāṇi citravartanayā kramāt

plain_english: Forms resting on the Vedas, or merely circular, or with clear horn, one should make, or in reverse order.
sanskrit_cite: vedāśrāyatarūpāṇi yadivā vṛttamātrataḥ spaṣṭaśṛṅgamatho kuryādyadivā vaiparītyataḥ

plain_english: Having broken the upward-facing or moon-pair, make four; crooked in the middle, clear downward-facing, situated at the side.
sanskrit_cite: unmukhaṃ candrayugmaṃ vā bhaṅktvā kuryāccatuṣṭayam kuṭilo madhyataḥ spaṣṭo@dhomukhaḥ pārśvagaḥ sthitaḥ

plain_english: Upright, half-equal, full, joined, and knot-placed; thus the moon's turning is twelvefold and delusion-breaking.
sanskrit_cite: uttāno@rdho@samaḥ pūrṇaḥ śliṣṭo granthigatastathā candrasyetthaṃ dvādaśadhā vartanā bhramabhedinī

plain_english: By inward and outward facing, she is again considered twofold; from those divisions of circles there would be countless expansion of divisions.
sanskrit_cite: antarbahirmukhatvena sā punardvividhā matā tadbhedānmaṇḍalānāṃ syādasaṅkhyo bhedavistaraḥ

plain_english: The mandala's lines vary through the blending of beauty and adornment.
sanskrit_cite: pīṭhavīthībahiarbhūmikaṇṭhakarṇakapolataḥ śobhopaśobhāsaṃbhedādguṇarekhāvikalpataḥ

plain_english: The circles become countless through variations of existence and nonexistence.
sanskrit_cite: svastikadvitayādyaṣṭatayāparyantabhedataḥ bhāvābhāvavikalpena maṇḍalānāmanantatā

plain_english: Then powders are given according to beauty: vermilion, lapis, and white chalk.
sanskrit_cite: tato rajāṃsi deyāni yathāśobhānusārataḥ sindūraṃ rājavartaṃ ca khaṭikā ca sitottamā

plain_english: Excellent powders here arise through union of three deities.
sanskrit_cite: uttamāni rajāṃsīha devatātrayayogataḥ parā candrasamaprakhyā raktā devī parāparā

plain_english: All goddesses dance always when they see this circle.
sanskrit_cite: aparā sā parā kālī bhīṣaṇā caṇḍayoginī dṛṣṭvaitanmaṇḍalaṃ devyaḥ sarvā nṛtyanti sarvadā

plain_english: Even without worship, seeing the circle initiates one through the mothers.
sanskrit_cite: anarcite@pyadīkṣeṇa dṛṣṭe dīkṣyeta mātṛbhiḥ kiṃvātibahunoktena tritriśūlārasaptakāḥ

plain_english: The supreme goddess power is established as breath-bearing among the trident rites.
sanskrit_cite: śūlayāgāḥ ṣaṭ sahasrāṇyevaṃ sārdhaśatadvayam yā sā devī parā śaktiḥ prāṇavāhā vyavasthitā

plain_english: The world is established in this coil through principles and their goddesses.
sanskrit_cite: viśvāntaḥ kuṇḍalākārā sā sākṣādatra vartitā tattvāni tattvadevyaśca viśvamasminpratiṣṭhitam

plain_english: Three trident-piercing powers sit above as seat, accomplishing enjoyment and liberation.
sanskrit_cite: atrordhve tantumātreṇa tisraḥ śūlāragāḥ sthitāḥ āsanatvena cecchādyā bhogamokṣaprasādhikāḥ

plain_english: Therefore one desiring liberation worships this great rite with great splendor.
sanskrit_cite: tāstu mokṣaikakāmasya śūlārāviddhamadhyakāḥ tasmādenaṃ mahāyāgaṃ mahāvibhavavistaraiḥ

plain_english: By merely seeing this circle, spirits, vetalas, and guhyakas flee.
sanskrit_cite: pūjayedbhūtikāmo vā mokṣakāmo@pivā budhaḥ asya darśanamātreṇa bhūtavetālaguhyakāḥ

plain_english: Even one weak in power pleases Shiva directly through worship of this circle.
sanskrit_cite: palāyante daśa diśaḥ śivaḥ sākṣātprasīdati mandaśaktibalāviddho@pyetanmaṇḍalapūjanāt

plain_english: Always by six months one attains trika knowledge, having obtained and considered by oneself what is to be rejected and accepted.
sanskrit_cite: satataṃ māsaṣaṭkena trikajñānaṃ samaśnute yatprāpya heyopādeyaṃ svayameva vicārya saḥ

plain_english: At the end of the body one becomes Bhairava-self; one desiring siddhi succeeds in this mandala through pervasion and deity placement.
sanskrit_cite: dehānte syādbhairavātmā siddhikāmo@tha siddhyati maṇḍalasyāsya yo vyāptiṃ devatānyāsameva ca

plain_english: He knows conduct as guru in trika teaching; his foot-dust is to be borne on the head by one desiring Shiva.
sanskrit_cite: vartanāṃ ca vijānāti sa gurustrikaśāsane tasya pādarajo mūrdhni dhāryaṃ śivasamīhinā

plain_english: Here worship creation, preservation, and destruction in order; the fourth, however, is all-filling from the middle, or in all.
sanskrit_cite: atra sṛṣṭisthitidhvaṃsān kramāt trīnapi pūjayet turyaṃ tu madhyato yadvā sarveṣu paripūrakam

plain_english: Or perform the four-trident or hidden-staff sacrifice; there worship that fourfold sequence properly and clearly.
sanskrit_cite: catustriśūlaṃ vā guptadaṇḍaṃ yāgaṃ samācaret tatra tat pūjayetsamyak sphuṭaṃ kramacatuṣṭayam

plain_english: Thus this was told in the secret supreme sixfold heart, declared and indicated in Siddhayogishvari-mata.
sanskrit_cite: ityetatkathitaṃ gupte ṣaḍardhahṛdaye pare ṣaṭke proktaṃ sūcitaṃ śrīsiddhayogīśvarīmate

plain_english: Having threaded the mandala in front, it grants all desires, equipped with great trident and adorned with lotus wheel.
sanskrit_cite: agrataḥ sūtrayitvā tu maṇḍalaṃ sarvakāmadam mahāśūlasamopetaṃ padmacakrādibhūṣitam

plain_english: At each gate draw a trident, excluding the western; or in corners make a great trident with tree.
sanskrit_cite: dvāre dvāre likhecchūlaṃ varjayitvā tu paścimam koṇeṣvapica vā kāryaṃ mahāśūlaṃ drumānvitam

plain_english: At the trident tip place trika; thus it is to be made eightfold, or threefold.
sanskrit_cite: amṛtāmbhobhavārīṇāṃ śūlāgre tu trikaṃ trikam śūla itthaṃ prakartavyamaṣṭadhā tat tridhāpivā

plain_english: Thus the divine city of sky-goers is indicated; it is told in Siddha-tantra teaching, even in another place.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ saṃsūcitaṃ divyaṃ khecarīṇāṃ puraṃ tviti sthānāntare@pi kathitaṃ śrīsiddhātantraśāsane

plain_english: Lotus-born in the middle, with trident peaks by its half; the trident-marked mandala is to be constructed, and lotus-marked in filling.
sanskrit_cite: kajaṃ madhye tadardhena śūlaśṛṅgāṇi tāni tu śūlāṅkaṃ maṇḍalaṃ kalpyaṃ kamalāṅkaṃ ca pūraṇe

plain_english: Now the trident-lotus arrangement is in Shripurva, Trishira-mata, Siddha-tantra, Trikakula, and Devi-yamala-mala.
sanskrit_cite: atha śūlābjavinyāsaḥ śrīpūrve triśiromate siddhātantre trikakule devyāyāmalamālayoḥ

plain_english: As stated in the essence treatise, the existence and secrets of tantra are shown clearly, even though the order has been stated before.
sanskrit_cite: yathoktaḥ sāraśāstre ca tantrasadbhāvaguhyayoḥ tathā pradarśyate spaṣṭaṃ yadyapyuktakramādgataḥ

plain_english: In the veda-supported three-hand measure, first divide the eastern half, abandoning all sides, toward east, north, and south.
sanskrit_cite: vedāśrite trihaste prāk pūrvamardha vibhājayet hastārdhaṃ sarvatastyaktvā pūrvodagyāmyadiggatam

plain_english: With three-finger upward slanting eightfold cells, abandon two and two parts, then proceed again south and north.
sanskrit_cite: tryaṅgulaiḥ koṣṭhakairūrdhvaistiryak cāṣṭadvidhātmakaiḥ dvau dvau bhāgau parityajya punardakṣiṇasaumyagau

plain_english: From Brahma's side, from the fourth living side eastward, a half-part measure gives two moon-segment pairs.
sanskrit_cite: brahmaṇaḥ pārśvayorjīvāccaturthāt pūrvatastathā bhāgārdhabhāgamānaṃ tu khaṇḍacandradvayaṃ dvayam

plain_english: In the third between them, on the south and north sides, in the living principle, the wise one makes a pair of moon segments by inner rotation.
sanskrit_cite: tayorantastṛtīye tu dakṣiṇottarapārśvayoḥ jīve khaṇḍenduyugalaṃ kuryādantarbhramādbudhaḥ

plain_english: At the farther vital point, reaching the tips of two moon segments, one makes an outward-facing rotation and two moon-segment pairs.
sanskrit_cite: tayoraparamarmasthaṃ khaṇḍendudvayakoṭigam bahirmukhaṃ bhramaṃ kuryāt khaṇḍacandradvayaṃ dvayam

plain_english: Similarly in Brahma, one does the part and half-part measure, then at the end of the second part on both sides.
sanskrit_cite: tadvadbrahmaṇi kurvīta bhāgabhāgārdhasaṃmitam tato dvitīyabhāgānte brahmaṇaḥ pārśvayordvayoḥ

plain_english: Two eastern-going lines are led by wise ones in third-part equality to the tip of the half-moon above, joined to Brahma's thread tip.
sanskrit_cite: dve rekhe pūrvage neye bhāgatryaṃśaśame budhaiḥ ekārdhendūrdhvakoṭisthaṃ brahmasūtrāgrasaṅgatam

plain_english: One should make two threads for establishing the middle peak; one thread is held in one interval from the living side of that tip.
sanskrit_cite: sūtradvayaṃ prakurvīta madhyaśṛṅgaprasiddhaye tadagrapārśvayorjīvāt sūtramekāntare dhṛtam

plain_english: Bring to the corner end from the corner of the first and second moon segments, and from the farther living side and the corner of the first half-moon.
sanskrit_cite: ādidvitīyakhaṇḍendukoṇāt koṇāntamānayet tayorevāparājjīvāt prathamārdhendukoṇataḥ

plain_english: Just so, lead the thread for establishing two peaks; in the other half of the field there is a staff of two hands, hidden five.
sanskrit_cite: tadvadeva nayetsūtraṃ śṛṅgadvitayasiddhaye kṣetrārdhe cāpare daṇḍo dvikaraśchannapañcakaḥ

plain_english: The six-spread four-long measure, with vedic finger below it and impurity essence, has its root below; a sharp tip is desired.
sanskrit_cite: ṣaḍvistṛtaṃ caturdīrghaṃ tadadho@malasārakam vedāṅgulaṃ ca tadadho mūlaṃ tīkṣṇāgramiṣyate

plain_english: For the first field, make four gates in the directions, measuring a cubit or half, or equal to the breadth.
sanskrit_cite: ādikṣetrasya kurvīta dikṣu dvāracatuṣṭayam hastāyāmaṃ tadardhaṃ vā vistārādapi tatsamam

plain_english: Outside, make the lotus double; listen, make circles with single-part measures in a veda-like manner.
sanskrit_cite: dviguṇaṃ bāhyataḥ kuryāttataḥ padmaṃ yathā śṛṇu ekaikabhāgamānāni kuryādvṛttāni vedavat

plain_english: In the directions eight, and again eight, life threads; sixteen in all, drop the numbered ones in the middle of each pair.
sanskrit_cite: dikṣvaṣṭau punarapyaṣṭau jīvasūtrāṇi ṣoḍaśa dvayordvayoḥ punarmadhye tatsaṃkhyātāni pātayet

plain_english: Make the whirling equal to the side life in the third circle, up to this point; then measure the life tip.
sanskrit_cite: eṣāṃ tṛtīyavṛttasthaṃ pārśvajīvasamaṃ bhramam etadantaṃ prakurvīta tato jīvāgramānayet

plain_english: Wherever contact is steadied in that connection, the mantra master acts there and leads the leaf tips to success.
sanskrit_cite: yatraiva kutracitsaṅgastatsaṃbandhe sthirīkṛte tatra kṛtvā nayenmantrī patrāgrāṇāṃ prasiddhaye

plain_english: In each petal make three and three filaments, double eight fingers to be made, and likewise three horns.
sanskrit_cite: ekaikasmindale kuryātkesarāṇāṃ trayaṃ trayam dviguṇāṣṭāṅgulaṃ kāryaṃ tadvacchṛṅgakajatrayam

plain_english: The pericarp is yellow; the filament net is made white, red, and yellow by root, middle, and tip.
sanskrit_cite: karṇikā pītavarṇena mūlamadhyāgrabhedataḥ sitaṃ raktaṃ tathā pītaṃ kāryaṃ kesarajālakam

plain_english: The petals are white; with the elephant goad, the seat is likewise four-cornered, half the pericarp, outside.
sanskrit_cite: dalāni śuklavarṇāni prativāraṇayā saha pīṭhaṃ tadvaccatuṣkoṇaṃ karṇikārdhasamaṃ bahiḥ

plain_english: The feet are white, red, yellow, black from fire in order; four horns, and three circles are intended.
sanskrit_cite: sitaraktapītakṛṣṇaistatpādān vahnitaḥ kramāt caturbhirapi śṛṅgāṇi tribhirmaṇḍalamiṣyate

plain_english: The staff should be blue-red with yellow amala essence; make the red trident as previously appointed.
sanskrit_cite: daṇḍaḥ syānnīlaraktena pītamāmalasārakam raktaṃ śūlaṃ prakurvīta yattatpūrvaṃ prakalpitam

plain_english: Behind the gate, in front, leaving four fingers, make the gate veda-cornered, round, mixed, or variegated.
sanskrit_cite: paścāddvārasya pūrveṇa tyaktvāṅgulacatuṣṭayam dvāraṃ vedāśri vṛttaṃ vā saṃkīrṇaṃ vā vicitritam

plain_english: The one-two-three city is equal, joined or both, and variegated with cheek, throat, beauty, adornment, and many decorations.
sanskrit_cite: ekadvitripuraṃ tulyaṃ sāmudgamathavobhayam kapolakaṇṭhaśobhopaśobhādibahucitritam

plain_english: Thus it is said in the Shridevyayamala: the field has a varied arrangement and is endowed with fine vine-houses, when the veda-supported field exists.
sanskrit_cite: vicitrākārasaṃsthānaṃ vallīsūkṣmagṛhānvitam śrīdevyāyāmale tūktaṃ kṣetre vedāśrite sati

plain_english: Having made half twelve-fold, horizontally and vertically, the teacher should lower one horizontal portion upward from his own side.
sanskrit_cite: ardhaṃ dvādaśadhā kṛtvā tiryagūrdhvaṃ ca tiryajam bhāgamekaṃ svapārśvordhvaṃ guruḥ samavatārayet

plain_english: That middle three-part should be rotated at its end; abandoning one portion, one should rotate again in its middle.
sanskrit_cite: madhyasthaṃ taṃ tribhāgaṃ ca tadante bhramayedubhau bhāgamekaṃ parityajya tanmadhye bhramayetpunaḥ

plain_english: From the third part upward, rotating the upward part until the end; from the fourth part upward, but join up and down again.
sanskrit_cite: tṛtīyāṃśordhvato bhrāmyamūrdhvāṃśaṃ yāvadantataḥ caturthāṃśāttadūrdhvaṃ tu ūrdhvādho yojayetpunaḥ

plain_english: Rotating upward from that measure, one should appoint by the fourth; the thread joins upward in order up to the brahma-thread.
sanskrit_cite: tanmānādūrdhvamābhrāmya caturthena niyojayet ūrdhvādyojayate sūtraṃ brahmasūtrāvadhi kramāt

plain_english: Having made the portion by order and width, one should diminish it again; the staff is desired as double the half-portion measure.
sanskrit_cite: kramādvaipulyataḥ kṛtvā aṃśaṃ vai hrāsayet punaḥ ardhabhāgapramāṇastu daṇḍo dviguṇa iṣyate

plain_english: Taking portion by portion from both ranges, the rotating leaf becomes downward like a pippala leaf.
sanskrit_cite: bhāgaṃ bhāgaṃ gṛhītvā tu ubhayoratha gocarāt bhrāmyaṃ pippalavat patraṃ vartanaiṣā tvadho bhavet

plain_english: In the sixteenth part one should draw a lotus; by twelve-angula reduction, above that in the middle portion one should draw the lotus-birth well.
sanskrit_cite: ṣoḍaśāṃśe likhetpadmaṃ dvādaśāṅgulalopanāt tadūrdhvaṃ madhyabhāge tu vārijanma samālikhet

plain_english: At the end of the middle horn, one should draw the third; likewise here on right and left, one should draw well in the hip lotus.
sanskrit_cite: madhyaśṛṅgāvasāne tu tṛtīyaṃ vilikhettataḥ savyāsavye tathaiveha kaṭisthābje samālikhet

plain_english: The pericarp is yellowish; the filament is red, yellow, and white; and the petals placed outside the lotus are white, as counter-obstacle.
sanskrit_cite: karṇikā pītalā raktapītaśuklaṃ ca kesaram dalāni padmabāhyasthā śuklā ca prativāraṇī

plain_english: The trident is black powder; the brahma-line is white; the trident-tip is joined by flame; and the trident staff is yellowish.
sanskrit_cite: śūlaṃ kṛṣṇena rajasā brahmarekhā sitā punaḥ śūlāgraṃ jvālayā yuktaṃ śūladaṇḍastu pītalaḥ

plain_english: In the middle of the trident, in that lotus, the wise one should always worship the lord; above it the supreme, on the right, and another on the left.
sanskrit_cite: śūlamadhye ca yatpadmaṃ tatreśaṃ pūjayetsadā asyordhve tu parāṃ dakṣe@nyāṃ vāme cāparāṃ budhaḥ

plain_english: That goddess, beyond supreme time, established as time's end, always devours the trident wheel by mere will.
sanskrit_cite: yā sā kālāntakā devī parātītā vyavasthitā grasate śūlacakraṃ sā tvicchāmātreṇa sarvadā

plain_english: This power is peace-form and knowledge-form supreme; but foundation is lower, and cessation is both supreme and lower.
sanskrit_cite: śāntirūpā kalā hyeṣā vidyārūpā parā bhavet aparā tu pratiṣṭhā syānnivṛttistu parāparā

plain_english: The upward-standing Bhairava staff has Sada-Shiva nature; its four powers are gross and subtle in many ways.
sanskrit_cite: bhairavaṃ daṇḍa ūrdhvasthaṃ rūpaṃ sādāśivātmakam catasraḥ śaktayastvasya sthūlāḥ sūkṣmāstvanekadhā

plain_english: This sacrifice is called the Damara three-powered sacrifice; then the trident-lotus rite is described in Trishira.
sanskrit_cite: eṣa yāgaḥ samākhyāto ḍāmarākhyastriśaktikaḥ atha traiśirase śūlābjavidhirdṛṣṭo@bhilikhyate

plain_english: With principal purifiers such as left nectar, pleasing and purifying, worship the ground, dust, instrument, and chalk from the root.
sanskrit_cite: vāmāmṛtādibhirmukhyaiḥ pavitraiḥ sumanoramaiḥ bhūmiṃ rajāṃsi karaṇīṃ khaṭikāṃ mūlato@rcayet

plain_english: In a square four-cubit space, place the trident in the middle; it has three hands, fierce form, two cubits, and a large up-down seat pair.
sanskrit_cite: caturaśre caturhaste madhye śūlaṃ karatrayam caṇḍo dvihasta ūrdhvādhaḥpīṭhayugvipulastvasau

plain_english: The staff, eight fingers and with three threads, is to be made; at the staff root, the seat is twelve fingers.
sanskrit_cite: vasvaṅgulaḥ prakartavyaḥ sūtratrayasamanvitaḥ dvādaśāṅgulamānena daṇḍamūle tu pīṭhikā

plain_english: Upward from length and height, by four-finger measure; upward from height, four fingers; from length, ten fingers.
sanskrit_cite: dairghyāttūcchrāyāccordhve ca caturaṅgulamānataḥ ūrdhve@pyucchrāyato vedāṅgulā dairghyāddaśāṅgulā

plain_english: Having made the trident-root seat in the middle measured by space-ocean-equal fingers, make the staff a trident divided into three parts all around.
sanskrit_cite: śūlamūlagataṃ pīṭhīmadhyaṃ khābdhisamāṅgulam kṛtvā daṇḍaṃ triśūlaṃ tu tribhirbhāgaiḥ samantataḥ

plain_english: By eight-finger measure all around, the trident tip would be hand-measure; the middle and root become accordingly.
sanskrit_cite: aṣṭāṅgulapramāṇaiḥ syāddhastamātraṃ samantataḥ śūlāgraṃ śūlamadhyaṃ tacchūlamūlaṃ tu tadbhavet

plain_english: The altar is to be made in the middle; at both sides it is six fingers and twelve fingers long.
sanskrit_cite: vedī madhye prakartavyā ubhayośca ṣaḍaṅgulam dvādaśāṅguladīrghā tu ubhayoḥ pārśvayostathā

plain_english: From four-finger height at the root, arrange the altar; at both sides it is thus half-moon shaped.
sanskrit_cite: caturaṅgulamucchrāyānmūle vedīṃ prakalpayet ubhayoḥ pārśvayoścaivamardhacandrākṛtiṃ tathā

plain_english: Rotate the chalk thread around the waist, making it two fingers wide and four fingers long by measure, O goddess.
sanskrit_cite: bhrāmayet khaṭikāsūtraṃ kaṭiṃ kuryāddviraṅgulām vaipulyāddairghyato devi caturaṅgulamānataḥ

plain_english: Arrange the left side likewise as the right side, with one finger width from the trident tip in the middle, below and above.
sanskrit_cite: yādṛśaṃ dakṣiṇe bhāge vāme tadvatprakalpayet madhye śūlāgravaipulyādaṅgulaśca adhordhvataḥ

plain_english: By four-finger measure from width, six fingers from height, then the gaṇḍikā should be made by its own form.
sanskrit_cite: caturaṅgulamānena vaipulyāttu ṣaḍaṅgulā ucchrāyāttu tataḥ kāryā gaṇḍikā tu svarūpataḥ

plain_english: Above the base, O good-vowed one, the trident base should be made; the trident tip should be made one finger, very sharp, six fingers.
sanskrit_cite: pīṭhordhve tu prakartavyaṃ śūlamūlaṃ tu suvrate śūlāgramaṅgulaṃ kāryaṃ sutīkṣṇaṃ tu ṣaḍaṅgulam

plain_english: The hub middle should be made; below the hub, six fingers, four fingers deep, and the middle should be arranged.
sanskrit_cite: arāmadhyaṃ prakartavyamarādhastu ṣaḍaṅgulam caturaṅgulanimnaṃ tu madhyaṃ tu parikalpayet

plain_english: East-west, that trident in the middle; outside that, make with three threads, turning them one by one.
sanskrit_cite: pūrvāparaṃ tadeveha madhye śūlaṃ tu tadbahiḥ kārayeta tribhiḥ sūtrairekaikaṃ vartayeta ca

plain_english: Three lotuses at the trident tip, twelve fingers by Veda parts, in order right, middle, left, with three, eight, and twelve petals.
sanskrit_cite: kajatrayaṃ tu śūlāgraṃ vedāṃśairdvādaśāṅgulam kramāddakṣānyamadhyeṣu tryaṣṭadvādaśapatrakam

plain_english: Three wheels, wind city, an eight-finger lotus called vidyā at the trident base; scatter powder afterward.
sanskrit_cite: cakratrayaṃ vātapuraṃ padmamaṣṭāṅgulārakam vidyābhikhyaṃ śūlamūle rajaḥ paścātprapātayet

plain_english: Fill the trident up to the staff with rājavarta; on the back of the three threads, three white lines should be.
sanskrit_cite: triśūlaṃ daṇḍaparyantaṃ rājavartena pūrayet sūtratrayasya pṛṣṭhe tu śuklaṃ cārātrayaṃ bhavet

plain_english: With white powder at the trident base, the vidyā lotus should be; upward in order, three lotuses are red, red-black, white.
sanskrit_cite: śuklena rajasā śūlamūle vidyāmbujaṃ bhavet raktaṃ raktāsitaṃ śuklaṃ kramādūrdhvāmbujatrayam

plain_english: The sky line should be white, one finger thick; leaving that outside, the platform should be made hand measure by measure.
sanskrit_cite: śuklena vyomarekhā syāt sā sthaulyādaṅgulaṃ bahiḥ tāṃ tyaktvā vedikā kāryā hastamātraṃ pramāṇātaḥ

plain_english: The wall should be square, three times the width from length; then all around, in directions, doors should be hand measure.
sanskrit_cite: vaipulyatriguṇaṃ dairghyāt prākāraṃ caturaśrakam samantato@tha dikṣu syurdvārāṇi karamātrataḥ

plain_english: Divide the twelve-angula measure gradually into three parts: neck, cheek, beauty, and ornament at the end.
sanskrit_cite: tridhā vibhajya kramaśo dvādaśāṅgulamānataḥ kaṇṭhaṃ kapolaṃ śobhāṃ tu upaśobhāṃ tadantataḥ

plain_english: Then make a square wall furnished with lines, using white, red, yellow, and black powders.
sanskrit_cite: prākāraṃ caturaśraṃ tu sabhūrekhāsamanvitam sitaraktapītakṛṣṇai rajobhiḥ kārayettataḥ

plain_english: Fill the middle with red powders as befits beauty, and follow there what was said earlier about its pervasion.
sanskrit_cite: raktai rajobhirmadhyaṃ tu yathāśobhaṃ tu pūrayet asyā vyāptau purā coktaṃ tatraivānusarecca tat

plain_english: Night-day division, entry, exit, rotation, pervasion of the anahata place, and the supreme rise of kundali are listed.
sanskrit_cite: arātrayavibhāgastu praveśo nirgamo bhramaḥ anāhatapadavyāptiḥ kuṇḍalyā udayaḥ paraḥ

plain_english: The trident goddesses are in the heart place; the trident staff stands at the navel; the trident root is situated in the heart.
sanskrit_cite: hṛdi sthāne gatā devyastriśūlasya sumadhyame nābhisthaḥ śūladaṇḍastu śūlamūlaṃ hṛdi sthitam

plain_english: Remember the three wheels at the end, lifting repeatedly by kala from the form of the body's middle.
sanskrit_cite: śaktisthānagataṃ prāntaṃ prānte cakratrayaṃ smaret utkṣipyotkṣipya kalayā dehamadhyasvarūpataḥ

plain_english: Having traversed the trident staff and trident middle-end ranges, enter root, middle, and end into the shakti abode at the final end.
sanskrit_cite: śūladaṇḍāntamadhyasthaśūlamadhyāntagocaram praviśenmūlamadhyāntaṃ prāntānte śaktiveśmani

plain_english: After making non-pulsation, once turning pulsation and pressing root bliss, one should enter the place of the three shaktis.
sanskrit_cite: aspandakaraṇaṃ kṛtvā ekadā spandavartanam mūlamānandamāpīḍya śaktitrayapadaṃ viśet

plain_english: There, with effortful worship, all siddhis arise from union of all paths and from sixfold path pervasion.
sanskrit_cite: tatra pūjyaṃ prayatnena jāyante sarvasiddhayaḥ samastādhvasamāyogāt ṣoḍhādhvavyāptibhāvataḥ

plain_english: With effort of all mantra wheels and so on, one should contemplate the trident made of thirty-six tattvas.
sanskrit_cite: samastamantracakrādyairevamādiprayatnataḥ ṣaṭtriṃśattattvaracitaṃ triśūlaṃ paribhāvayet

plain_english: At equinox, place the mantras in the supreme mandala; when this is worshipped, one attains the place of the all-lord.
sanskrit_cite: viṣuvatsthena vinyāso mantrāṇāṃ maṇḍalottame kāryo@smin pūjite yatra sarveśvarapadaṃ bhajet

plain_english: With svastika the fitting rite is to be done; place the channels first, according to muhurta measure.
sanskrit_cite: svastikenātha kartavyaṃ yuktaṃ tasyocyate vidhiḥ nāḍikāḥ sthāpayetpūrvaṃ muhūrtaṃ parimāṇataḥ

plain_english: Twenty-nine lineages are located in the indra, varuna, south, and north directions, going straight and transverse.
sanskrit_cite: śakravāruṇadiksthāśca yāmyasaumyagatāstathā ekonatriṃśadvaṃśāḥ syurṛjutiryaggatāstathā

plain_english: Eight hundred forty-one marman points arise by lineages and sense counts in the lotus circle.
sanskrit_cite: aṣṭau marmaśatānyekacatvāriṃśacca jāyate vaṃśairviṣayasaṃkhyaiśca padmaṃ yugmendumaṇḍalam

plain_english: By taste counts the seat becomes a svastika giving all desires; by vasu counts the door paths are arranged.
sanskrit_cite: rasasaṃkhyairbhavetpīṭhaṃ svastikaṃ sarvakāmadam vasusaṃkhyairdvāravīthāvevaṃ bhāgaparikramaḥ

plain_english: Destroy the holes, brahmin, arrow, and fire points, outer and inner, in order, in four directions and middle doors, O beautiful one.
sanskrit_cite: randhravipraśarāgnīṃśca lupyedbāhyāntaraṃ kramāt marmāṇi ca caturdikṣu madhyāddvāreṣu sundari

plain_english: In cities of fire, earth, sage, sky, outer, and womb, destroy marman points devoid of inner channels.
sanskrit_cite: vahnibhūtamunivyomabāhyagarbhe purīṣu ca lopayeccaiva marmāṇi antarnāḍivivarjitān

plain_english: In door and wall corners, channels of brahma lineage situated from eye and taste, including eye, fire, arrow, and seasons, are to be destroyed.
sanskrit_cite: dvāraprākārakoṇeṣu netrānalaśarānṛtūn nāḍayo brahmavaṃśasya lopyā netrādrasasthitāḥ

plain_english: Destroy fire and eye-fire; vedas and eye-pair from taste; the moon-going eye; and east vedas fire from taste.
sanskrit_cite: vahnernetrānalau lopyau vedānnetrayugaṃ rasāt netraṃ saumyagataṃ lopyaṃ pūrvādvedānalau rasāt

plain_english: Abandoning the world-located small channel, eye vedas fires follow in order; also the arrow fire-going pair and eye fires from taste.
sanskrit_cite: lokasthā nāḍikā hitvā netrādvedāgnayaḥ kramāt śarairvahnigataṃ caiva yugaṃ netrāgnayo rasāt

plain_english: From the eye, the east-going is named sumeru door; svastika and pleasant city are located in four directions, both.
sanskrit_cite: netrāt pūrvagatāccaiva sumerurdvārasaṃjñitaḥ svastikā ca purī ramyā caturdikṣu sthitāvubhau

plain_english: Two hundred marman points, directions multiplied by sages, and eye-beginning parts are swept from the path middle, O beautiful one.
sanskrit_cite: marmaṇāṃ ca śate dve ca ṛṣibhirguṇitā diśaḥ netrādikāṃśca saṃmārjya mārgamadhyāt suśobhane

plain_english: Made by three sages in the middle, by senses the pericarp becomes; eye-made vasus, petal, and eye are once divided.
sanskrit_cite: ṛṣitrayakṛte madhye viṣayaiḥ karṇikā bhavet netrīkṛtānvasūn patraṃ netraṃ sakṛdvibhājitam

plain_english: Having made fire vasu-going, destroy moon-located points; in fires and sage middle, destroy up to seat and moon.
sanskrit_cite: vahniṃ vasugataṃ kṛtvā śaśāṅkasthāṃśca lopayet vahnīṣuṛṣimadhyācca lopyaṃ pīṭhendukāvadhi

plain_english: It speaks of removing brahman's eye-objects and omitting a small eye among eastward channels in the ocean.
sanskrit_cite: brahmaṇo netraviṣayānnetrādvedānalau haret sāgare netrakaṃ lopyaṃ nāḍayaḥ pūrvadiggatāḥ

plain_english: It directs omission in the four corners of the seat from the head and eye triad.
sanskrit_cite: bhūtanetragatānmūrdhnā netrāddvivahnidṛktrikāt saumyagāt pīṭhakoṇeṣu lopayeta caturṣvapi

plain_english: Petals are white, filaments red and yellow, the pericarp gold-like, and leaf tips red.
sanskrit_cite: dalāni kāryāṇi sitaiḥ kesaraṃ raktapītalaiḥ karṇikā kanakaprakhyā pallavāntāśca lohitāḥ

plain_english: The sky line is very white, and the seat is endowed with three lines: white, red, and yellow.
sanskrit_cite: vyomarekhā tu susitā vartulābjāntanīlabhāḥ pīṭhaṃ rekhātrayopetaṃ sitalohitapītalam

plain_english: Four-colored swastikas lie toward fire and northeast; a coral-like path and weapons are outside.
sanskrit_cite: svastikāśca caturvarṇā agnerīśānagocarāḥ vīthī vidrumasaṃkāśā svadikṣvastrāṇi bāhyataḥ

plain_english: It describes a sapphire-like thunderbolt, power, lotus-gem radiance, a gold-like staff, and a very red face.
sanskrit_cite: indranīlanibhaṃ vajraṃ śaktiṃ padmamaṇiprabhām daṇḍaṃ hāṭakasaṃkāśaṃ vaktraṃ tasyātilohitam

plain_english: A blue-radiant sword, a calf-shining noose, and a banner adorned with flowers, fruits, and five colors are described.
sanskrit_cite: nīladyutisamaṃ khaḍgaṃ pāśaṃ vatsakasaprabham dhvajaṃ puṣpaphalopetaṃ pañcaraṅgaiśca śobhitam

plain_english: The mace is gold-like, fierce, and gem-adorned; the trident is blue-lotus-like with a blazing fiery crest.
sanskrit_cite: gadā hemanibhātyugrā nānāratnavibhūṣitā śūlaṃ nīlāmbujasamaṃ jvaladvahnyugraśekharam

plain_english: Above it is a white lotus and a gold-like wheel with radiant beryl-like spokes.
sanskrit_cite: tasyopari sitaṃ padmamīṣatpītāruṇaprabham cakraṃ hemanibhaṃ dīptamarā vaiḍūryasaṃnibhāḥ

plain_english: The temple of the god of gods has a very yellow spoke-middle and flame-red outer part, granting all desired fruits.
sanskrit_cite: arāmadhyaṃ supītaṃ ca bāhyaṃ jvālāruṇaṃ bhavet mandiraṃ devadevasya sarvakāmaphalapradam

plain_english: The trident rite is first performed in a square field of hand measure, divided in three ways.
sanskrit_cite: śrīsiddhāyāṃ śūlavidhiḥ prāk kṣetre caturaśrite hastamātraṃ tridhā sūryānnavakhaṇḍaṃ yathā bhavet

plain_english: The middle part is divided in three ways with nine cells, and then this rite is described.
sanskrit_cite: madhye śūlaṃ ca tatretthaṃ madhyabhāgaṃ tridhā bhajet navabhiḥ koṣṭhakairyuktaṃ tato@yaṃ vidhirucyate

plain_english: After leaving three middle parts, rotate the thread below so that a crescent-moon shape results.
sanskrit_cite: madhyabhāgatrayaṃ tyaktvā madhye bhāgadvayasya tu adhastādbhrāmayetsūtraṃ śaśāṅkaśakalākṛti

plain_english: Rotate from both sides so a shape arises at the tip, then draw the former line there with the thread.
sanskrit_cite: ubhayato bhrāmayettatra yathāgre hākṛtirbhavet koṭyāṃ tatra kṛtaṃ sūtraṃ nayedrekhāṃ tu pūrvikām

plain_english: Leaving four fingers by the previous far gate, the wise one destroys the line so a trident shape results.
sanskrit_cite: aparadvārapūrveṇa tyaktvāṅgulacatuṣṭayam rekhāṃ vināśayetprājño yathā śūlākṛtirbhavet

plain_english: Leaving half a hand at the trident tip, make lotuses below, with three horns and a lotus with pericarp in the middle of the hand.
sanskrit_cite: śūlāgre tvardhahastena tyaktvā padmāni kārayet adhaḥ śṛṅgatrayaṃ hastamadhye padmaṃ sakarṇikam

plain_english: Hold the thread at the mouth tip, drop it in the middle with three hands, then make two fingers below.
sanskrit_cite: mukhāgre dhārayetsūtraṃ tribhirhastaistu pātayet madhye cordhvaṃ tataḥ kuryādadhastādaṅguladvayam

plain_english: Drop two lines so a trident forms; from the lower parts upward, the line reaches there.
sanskrit_cite: rekhādvayaṃ pātayeta yathā śūlaṃ bhavatyapi adhobhāgādibhiścordhvaṃ tatra rekhā prapadyate

plain_english: Having equalized the threads, place two upward; the middle lotus is to be established below the trident, O glorious one.
sanskrit_cite: samīkṛtya tataḥ sūtre ūrdhve dve evameva tu madhyaṃ padmaṃ pratiṣṭhāpyaṃ śūlādhastādyaśasvini

plain_english: Thus this mandala rite has been spoken in concise form by the great teachers.
sanskrit_cite: ityeṣa maṇḍalavidhiḥ kathitaḥ saṃkṣepayogato mahāgurubhiḥ
